text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israeli and Palestinian negotiators struggle to save Middle East peace process.
- Select Committee on Health Care Subsidy conclude Singapore Democratic Party and its chairman Ling How Doong have no basis to make their claim that health care is hardly subsidised.
- Singapore's leading female banker, Elizabeth Sam, becomes first woman to win seat on the board of a Big Four local bank with appointment as director and deputy president of OCBC Bank.
- Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp expects to launch fourth industrial park in either Java or the Philippines costing about US$425 million.
- Sinar Mas will put some of its oil palm estates and noodle factory assets into Amcol Holdings, which is to be renamed Golden Amcol.
- Malaysia's Ekran Bhd signs six-year key deal with Swiss-based Asea Brown Boveri AG to bukld the Malaysian $13.6 billion Bakun dam.
- Singapore company Third Dragon Development Pte Ltd in expansion plan involving building of US$300 million theme park and development of a 50 million yuan orchard.
- Labroy Marine launch initial public offering of 52 million shares at issue price of Singapore 69 cents each to raise Singapore $19.65 million.
- Transport group Tibs Holdings enters into agreement to set up joint-venture company in China with a state-owned company to design and make coach chassis and trucks.
- KYZ Zenith Hotels International, in which Hai Sun Hup has 50 percent stake, wins management of Grand Sun Hotel in China.
